response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Scope the retry-exhaustion delete to unscheduled SMS reminders

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-43

Explanation:
In the new `deleteMany`, the `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition sits only inside the first `OR` branch. The second branch, `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, has no `method` filter and no `scheduled` filter. As a result, this SMS cron deletes every `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1`, whatever its method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS) and whether or not it was already scheduled.

Today only this handler increments `retryCount`, so the bug is latent. But the column is now shared across the whole model. Once another scheduler (email or WhatsApp) starts using it, this job will silently delete that scheduler's reminders.

It can also delete already-scheduled reminders whose `referenceId` is still needed for cancellation. The deletion is permanent and nothing is logged, so attendees simply never receive those reminders.

Fix:
- Move the `method` filter to the top level of the `where`.
- Restrict the retry branch to `scheduled: false`.
- Consider logging exhausted reminders before deleting them.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
await prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({
  where: {
    method: WorkflowMethods.SMS,
    OR: [
      { scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } },
      { retryCount: { gt: 1 }, scheduled: false },
    ],
  },
});
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Guard the retry-count update in the catch block so one failure doesn't abort the batch

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:189-198

Explanation:
The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block is unprotected. It can throw in two likely cases:
- The original failure was a DB or connection error that persists.
- The row was deleted concurrently, which raises P2025 "Record to update not found".

If it throws, the rejection escapes the per-reminder loop. Every remaining reminder in the batch is skipped and the cron request fails. The original error is also never logged, because `console.log` runs after the failing `await`.

Before this change, the `catch` swallowed errors per reminder and the loop continued.

Fix: log the original error first, then wrap the bookkeeping update in its own try/catch. Alternatively, use `updateMany`, which does not throw when no row matches.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
} catch (error) {
  console.log(`Error scheduling SMS with error ${error}`);
  try {
    await prisma.workflowReminder.update({
      where: { id: reminder.id },
      data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } },
    });
  } catch (updateError) {
    console.log(`Failed to increment retryCount for reminder ${reminder.id}: ${updateError}`);
  }
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Test
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Add tests for the new retry and purge behavior

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-43
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-197

Explanation:
The change adds three new behaviors to a cron handler that sends real SMS, and none of them is tested:
- incrementing `retryCount` when Twilio returns no SID,
- incrementing `retryCount` when scheduling throws,
- permanently deleting reminders once `retryCount > 1`.

The threshold semantics, the method scoping and the failure of the catch-block update are all easy to get wrong silently.

Add handler tests with a mocked Prisma client and a mocked `scheduleSMS`, covering:
- A response without a SID increments `retryCount`.
- A thrown error increments `retryCount` and the loop continues.
- A reminder with `retryCount = 2` is deleted, while one with `retryCount = 1` is kept.
- A non-SMS reminder with a high `retryCount` is not deleted.
- A rejection from the catch-block `update` does not stop processing of the remaining reminders.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
it("increments retryCount when scheduleSMS throws and continues the loop", async () => {
  scheduleSMSMock.mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error("twilio down")).mockResolvedValueOnce({ sid: "S1" });
  await handler(req, res);
  expect(prismaMock.workflowReminder.update).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    expect.objectContaining({ where: { id: 1 }, data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })
  );
  expect(prismaMock.workflowReminder.update).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    expect.objectContaining({ where: { id: 2 }, data: expect.objectContaining({ referenceId: "S1" }) })
  );
});
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Increment retryCount atomically instead of read-modify-write

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:179-186
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190-197

Explanation:
Both updates write `reminder.retryCount + 1`, a value computed from a snapshot read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (for example, a slow run and the next tick), both read the same value and both write the same `n+1`. One failure is lost, so the reminder is retried more often than intended.

Fix: use Prisma's `increment`, which is applied atomically in the database.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } },
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Consensus: 2/3 reviewers
Title: Replace the magic retry threshold with a named constant

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39-41

Explanation:
`gt: 1` hard-codes the retry policy, and the resulting sequence is easy to misread:
1. The first failure sets `retryCount` to 1.
2. The second failure sets it to 2.
3. The next run deletes the reminder, without any log entry.

So a reminder gets two attempts in total. Readers may take `1` to mean "1 retry", which hides a possible off-by-one. Tests would also have to duplicate the number.

Fix:
- Extract the threshold into a named, exported constant and use it in both the query and the tests.
- Confirm the intended number of attempts.
- Consider logging when a reminder is abandoned.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
export const MAX_SMS_RETRIES = 1; // reminder is deleted once retryCount exceeds this
// ...
{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: MAX_SMS_RETRIES } },
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Avoid an unindexed scan on retryCount every cron run

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-43
- packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1000-1000

Explanation:
The bare `retryCount > 1` predicate in the `OR` cannot use the existing indexes on `bookingUid` or `workflowStepId`. It will likely cause a sequential scan of the whole `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron invocation, and that table grows with every booking.

Fix: scope the predicate by `method` and `scheduled` (see issue 1). If the table is large, also add a supporting index.

Proposed fix:
~~~prisma
@@index([method, scheduled, retryCount])
~~~
